1 (Original): A tool comprising: a working portion; 5 a driving portion spaced from the working portion; a support structure between the working portion and the driving portion wherein the support structure defines a passage way extending at least in part between the driving portion and the working portion; a fluid flow element having at least a flow element portion 10 extending between the driving portion and the working portion wherein the flow element portion includes a first wall adjacent the passage way.

2 (Original): The tool of claim 1 wherein the fluid flow element is a tube.

3 (Original): The tool of claim 2 wherein the tube is a fiber-reinforced plastic tube.

4 (Original): The tool of claim 1 wherein the working portion includes a sintered matrix segment supported by the support structure.

5 (Original): The tool of claim 4 wherein the fluid flow element extends to an area adjacent the segment.

6 (Original): The tool of claim 1 wherein the support structure is a saw blade core and wherein the fluid flow element is a plastic tube extending within the core.

7 (Original): The tool of claim 1 further including an element in fluid communication with the fluid flow element for changing flow characteristics of a fluid passing through the fluid flow element.

8 (Original): The tool of claim 1 further including a nozzle adjacent the working portion and fluidly coupled to the fluid flow element.

9 (Original): The tool of claim 1 further including a control element adjacent the fluid flow element for controlling flow of fluid in the fluid flow element.

10 (Original): The tool of claim 9 wherein the control element changes fluid flow in the fluid flow element from a first condition to a second condition.

11 (Original): The tool of claim 10 wherein the control element reduces a flow volume of the fluid.

12 (Original): The tool of claim 11 wherein the control element substantially stops the flow of fluid in the fluid flow element.

13 (Original): A blade for working on a work material: a working portion; a driving portion being operated on by a device for driving the blade; a blade support structure extending between the working portion and the driving portion and defining a recessed area extending at least in part between the driving portion and the working portion and including at least one wall defining at least part of the recessed area; and a fluid flow element positioned in at least part of the recessed area and having a fluid flow element wall adjacent the at least one wall.

14 (Original): The blade of claim 13 wherein the fluid flow element is formed from a non-metallic material.

15 (Original): The blade of claim 14 wherein the fluid flow element is formed from a plastic material.

16 (Original): The blade of claim 14 wherein the fluid flow element is a fiber-reinforced material.

17 (Original): The blade of claim 13 wherein the fluid flow element defines an enclosed channel having a first wall defining an opening in the area of the working portion.

18 (Original): The blade of claim 17 wherein the fluid flow element is tubular.

19 (Original): The blade of claim 13 wherein the blade support structure includes first and second planar elements.

20 (Original): The blade of claim 19 wherein the fluid flow element is positioned between the first and second planar elements.

21 (Original): The blade of claim 20 further including an internal element between the first and second planar elements wherein the internal element includes a recessed portion and wherein the fluid flow element extends at least partly within the recessed portion.

22 (Original): The blade of claim 21 wherein the fluid flow element is a tube between the first and second planar elements extending within the recessed portion.

23 (Original): The blade of claim 22 wherein the first and second planar elements are discs and wherein the internal element includes a disc portion and radially-extending projections from the disc portion and wherein the tube extends from an area adjacent the disc portion to an area adjacent the work portion.

24 (Original): The blade of claim 23 wherein the first and second planar discs and the internal element are bonded together and wherein the tube is bonded between the first and second planar discs.

25 (Original): The blade of claim 13 further including a flow changing element in fluid communication with the fluid flow element between the fluid flow element and the working portion.

26 (Original): The blade of claim 25 wherein the flow changing element includes a nozzle.

27 (Original): The blade of claim 26 wherein the nozzle changes the direction of fluid flow of a fluid from the fluid flow element.

28 (Original): The blade of claim 26 wherein the nozzle has a cross-sectional area less than a cross-sectional area of the fluid flow element.

29 (Original): The blade of claim 13 further including a flow control element in fluid communication with the fluid flow element.

30 (Original): The blade of claim 29 wherein the flow control element is configured to reduce a flow volume of fluid from the fluid flow element.

31 (Original): The blade of claim 30 wherein the flow control element is configured to substantially stop fluid flow.

32 (Original): The blade of claim 30 wherein the flow control element is configured to control flow fluid from the fluid flow element and to direct flow fluid in a selected direction.

33 (Original): The blade of claim 29 wherein the flow control element includes an actuating surface.

34 (Original): The blade of claim 33 wherein the actuating surface extends past the working portion.

35 (Original): The blade of claim 33 wherein the support structure extends between the working portion and driving portion and wherein the actuating surface extends in a first direction away from the support structure.

36 (Original): The blade of claim 35 wherein the actuating surface extends in a second direction at least partly different from a direction of movement of the blade.

37 (Original): The blade of claim 36 wherein the blade is configured to rotate about an axis and wherein the second direction is substantially perpendicular to the axis.

38 (Original): A tool guard comprising: a first wall portion extending in a first direction; second and third wall portions extending in respective directions different than the first direction and extending from spaced apart portions of the first wall portion and wherein the first and second wall portions define an area for receiving a portion of a tool; a fourth wall portion extending in the first direction and coupled to the second wall portion and wherein the fourth wall portion forms a channel extending in the first direction.

39 (Original): A saw blade guard comprising: a first wall portion extending in a first direction wherein the first direction is the same as a direction of movement of the saw blade; first and second side wall portions extending spaced apart from respective portions of the first wall portion so that the first and second side wall portions and the first wall portion taken together define a housing area for receiving a portion of a saw blade; a first channel on the first side wall portion extending at least partly between the first and second side wall portions and configured to allow fluid flow at least partly in the first direction.

40 (Original): The guard of claim 39 wherein the first direction is at least partly circular and wherein the first channel extends at least partly in an arc.

41 (Original): The guard of claim 40 wherein the first channel has a cross-section that is partly circular.

42 (Original): The guard of claim 39 further including a second channel on the second side wall portion.

43 (Original): The guard of claim 42 wherein the second channel has a cross-section that is partly circular.

44 (Original): The guard of claim 39 wherein the first wall portion is curved toward the first and second side wall portions.

45 (Original): The guard of claim 44 wherein the first wall portion is at least partly circular in cross-section.

46 (Original): The guard of claim 39 wherein the first wall portion includes a recessed portion between the first and second side wall portions.

47 (Original): The guard of claim 46 wherein the recessed portion is closer to the first side wall portion than to the second side wall portion.

48 (Original): The guard of claim 47 further including a second channel on the second side wall portion.

49 (Original): The guard of claim 39 wherein the first wall portion includes a surface portion extending into a space between the first and second side wall portions.

50 (Original): The guard of claim 49 wherein the surface portion is configured to be substantially aligned with the saw blade when the guard is positioned adjacent the blade.

51 (Original): The guard of claim 49 wherein the surface portion is substantially centered between the first and second side wall portions.

52 (Original): The guard of claim 39 wherein the first and second side wall portions extended least partly in the first direction and wherein the first side wall portion extends from the first wall portion approximately the same distance as the second side wall portion extends from the first wall portion.

53 (Original): The guard of claim 52 wherein the first and second side wall portions extend in the first direction a first distance and wherein the first and second side wall portions extend from the first wall portion approximately the same amount along the first distance.

54 (Original): The guard of claim 39 further including a collecting element adjacent to guard and wherein the first channel extends to the collecting element.

55 (Original): The guard of claim 54 wherein the first channel extends into the collecting element.

56 (Original): The guard of claim 39 wherein the first wall portion extends in the first direction substantially along an arc defined by a radius and wherein the first side wall portion extends a substantially constant distance along a radius over the length of the arc.

57 (Original): The guard of claim 56 wherein the substantially constant distance is less than approximately half the length of the radius.

58 (Original): The guard of claim 56 wherein the substantially constant distance is less than approximately 1/4 of the length of the radius.

59 (Original): The guard of claim 39 further including a second wall portion movable relative to the first wall portion for extending the first wall portion in the first direction.

60 (Original): A cutting blade comprising: a blade structure having first and second outside surfaces; a passage through an area between the first and second outside surfaces configured so as to allow fluid to flow in the passage; a wall structure formed from a first material defining an inlet in fluid communication with the passage; and a transition element in the inlet formed different from the first material.

61 (Original): The blade of claim 60 wherein the transition element is formed from a second material different from the first material.

62 (Original): The blade of claim 60 wherein the transition element is formed at a different time than when the first element is formed.

63 (Original): The blade of claim 61 wherein the blade structure is substantially circular and wherein the passage extends from an inner area of the blade structure to an outer area of the blade structure.

64 (Original): The blade of claim 63 wherein the blade inner area includes a center hole and wherein the passage extends from adjacent the center hole outward in a direction away from the center hole.

65 (Original): The blade of claim 64 wherein the transition element includes an angled portion allowing fluid to change directions within the transition element.

66 (Original): The blade of claim 65 wherein the transition element includes an elbow structure.

67 (Original): The blade of claim 66 wherein the elbow structure includes an inlet portion and an outlet portion wherein the inlet portion has an internal cross-sectional area larger than an internal cross-sectional area of the outlet portion.

68 (Original): The blade of claim 67 wherein the inlet portion includes a conical surface configuration.

69 (Original): The blade of claim 67 wherein the outlet portion includes a substantially circular flow channel.

70 (Original): The blade of claim 64 wherein the inner area of the blade structure is substantially flat and the transition element opens in a direction that is substantially perpendicular to the inner area of the blade structure.

71 (Original): The blade of claim 64 further including a plurality of transition elements spaced from the center hole.

72 (Original): The blade of claim 64 wherein the transition element includes at least two wall portions defining at least two openings into the transition element.

73 (Original): The blade of claim 72 wherein the two wall portions combined to form a first channel passing through the blade and coupled to a third channel extending between the first channel and an outlet of the transition element.

74 (Original): The blade of claim 64 wherein the transition element includes walls defining no more than a single inlet and no more than a single outlet.

75 (Original): The blade of claim 74 further including a passage way extending between the inlet and the outlet wherein the passage way has a curve between the inlet and outlet.

76 (Original): The blade of claim 74 wherein the inlet has a cross-sectional area larger than a cross-sectional area of the outlet.

77 (Original): The blade of claim 63 wherein the blade structure is substantially circular and the blade inner area includes a center hole and wherein the transition element is positioned at least partly within the center hole.

78 (Original): The blade of claim 77 wherein the transition element includes a wall defining an inner opening and a wall defining an outer opening farther from a center of the blade than the inner opening.

79 (Original): The blade of claim 78 further including a wall defining a cavity for containing fluid between the inner opening and the outer opening.

80 (Original): The blade of claim 79 wherein the wall defining the cavity includes a plurality of inlet openings and a plurality of outlet openings and a reservoir in between the inlet and the outlet openings.

81 (Original): The blade of claim 79 wherein the outer opening opens into an area within the passage.

82 (Original): The blade of claim 81 wherein the transition element is coupled to a tube in the blade.

83 (Original): The blade of claim 82 wherein the transition element and the tube are integral with each other.

84 (Original): The blade of claim 60 further including a leg portion extending away from the transition element having a channel in fluid communication with the inlet.

85 (Original): The blade of claim 84 further including a tube extending into the leg portion.

86 (Original): The tool comprising: a working portion of the tool for working on a work surface and a support structure for supporting the working portion of the tool; a first outside surface adjacent the support structure and a second outside surface spaced apart from the first outside surface; a passage through an area between the first and second outside surfaces configured so as to allow fluid to flow in the passage; a wall structure formed from a first material defining an inlet in the first outside surface wherein the inlet is in fluid communication with the passage; and a transition element in the inlet formed different from the first material.

87 (Original): The tool of claim 86 wherein the transition element includes a wall defining an opening wherein the opening extends in a direction different from a direction in which the passage extends.

88 (Original): The tool of claim 87 wherein the transition element includes a channel portion extending between the opening and the passage.

89 (Original): The tool of claim 88 wherein the channel portion includes a curved portion extending from the opening to the passage and wherein the opening and the passage extend at substantially right angles to each other.

90 (Original): The tool of claim 88 further including a tube in the passage coupled to the transition element.

91 (Original): The tool of claim 86 wherein the tool is a substantially circular cutting blade and the working portion of the tool is at a perimeter of the cutting blade and the transition element is positioned between a center of the blade and the working portion.

92 (Original): The tool of claim 91 further including a plurality of working portions, a plurality of passages and a separate transition element for each passage.

93 (Original): The tool of claim 92 further including a tube extending in each of the plurality of passages and coupled to and in fluid communication with a respective transition element.

94 (Original): The tool of claim 91 wherein the cutting blade includes a wall defining an opening and wherein the transition element extends in a closed circuit adjacent the opening wall.

95 (Original): The tool of claim 94 wherein transition element has a substantially circular portion with a plurality of inlet openings and a plurality of outlet openings positioned outward relative to the inlet openings.

96 (Original): A cutting blade core comprising: a substantially circular blade core formed from first and second substantially spaced apart blade elements; at least one passage way extending within an area between the first and second substantially spaced apart blade elements and configured to allow fluid to flow in the passage way; a wall structure formed from a first material defining an inlet and in fluid communication with the passage way; and an inlet fitting in the inlet formed different from the first material.

97 (Original): The blade core of claim 96 wherein the first material is a metal and the inlet fitting is formed from a plastic.

98 (Original): The blade core of claim 96 wherein the wall structure forming the inlet is formed in the first blade element and wherein the inlet fitting includes an angled portion extending between an opening in the inlet and an outlet opening within the passage.

99 (Original): The blade core of claim 96 wherein the wall structure forming the inlet includes portions of the first and second blade elements adjacent an opening in the circular blade and wherein the inlet fitting extends in the opening and includes at least one outlet opening within the passage way.

100 (Original): The blade core of claim 99 further including a tubular structure within the passage way and coupled to the inlet fitting.

101 (Original): A tool comprising: a support structure for supporting a working portion and defining a recess for allowing fluid to flow from the support structure toward the working portion; a fluid changing portion in fluid communication with the fluid flow recess for changing a characteristic of a fluid before the fluid exits the support structure.

102 (Original): The tool of claim 101 wherein the fluid changing portion directs the fluid in the direction substantially parallel to a portion of the recess.

103 (Original): The tool of claim 101 wherein the fluid changing portion changes a fluid cross-sectional area from a first cross-sectional area to a second cross-sectional area.
